title: Rapid Rescue: Seller Sprint for Escalations and Recovery (v0.3)
content:
Overview
---
Purpose: Quick, actionable playdeck for sellers + SEs to triage, stabilize, and convert deals at risk due to latency/cost/regulatory objections. Focus: 20-minute call readiness, 60-minute tech follow-up plan, and handoff checklist to Solutions Engineering.
Audience: Field sellers, Solutions Engineers, AE + CSM for midmarket & enterprise deals.
Tone: tactical scripts, checklists, data points, and escalation paths — intentionally pragmatic.

Slide 1 — TL;DR (for quick prep)
- When to use: customer flags >2x expected latency, token cost shock, or network/data residency concerns during POC.
- Immediate goals: 1) calm the customer; 2) show measurable mitigation; 3) create a short timeline to remediate or provide a fallback.
- Key hooks to convert risk into value: Reserved capacity trial, Private deployment pilot, fast-fallback policy.

Slide 2 — Quick battle metrics to memorize (seller friendly)
- Typical hosted latencies: 50–250ms (short completions) / 300–1200ms (chat with history) — cite internal perf bench (Q4 2025).
- Cost ballpark: 1M tokens ~ $X hosted vs ~Y on Dedicated (show approximate multipliers). (Use real-time calc in demo)
- Conversion triggers: sustained load >500 qps or >$10k/mo spend -> Reserved discussion; compliance/regulatory -> Private.
Speaker note: don't waffle on numbers — use: "our telemetry shows X for this workload; we can run a tailored microbenchmark in 48h."

Slide 3 — 20-minute call script (starter)
1) Open: acknowledgement + empathy: "I hear this feels worse than expected — we'll get a reproducible plan."
2) Quick repro ask (under 3 min): "Can you share one request example, average sequence length, and whether embeddings/rerank used?"
3) Reassurance + immediate mitigation: "We can switch routing to Dedicated fallback or enable prefix-caching; both are reversible and low risk."
4) Next steps: "We will run a focused perf test and return with a remediation plan within 48 hours."

Slide 4 — Repro checklist for SE (what to capture in 20 mins)
- Exact request JSON / prompt + sample tokens
- Model name + pinned version (if any)
- Sequence length distribution (p90, median)
- Concurrent QPS during issue
- Whether streaming/stop tokens used
- Any policy/region constraints (data residency, IP allowlist)
- Business impact: features blocked, user-visible errors, cost delta

Slide 5 — Short technical mitigations (fast wins)
- Route to near-term Dedicated pool (if customer has reserved or trial) -> immediate latency stabilization.
- Enable prefix/KV caching on repeated prompts (saves up to 60–80% tokens for similar queries).
- Aggressive sequence truncation + summarization before model call.
- Lower precision / quantized model variant to reduce GPU memory pressure (trade quality).
- Fallback model with identical API surface + lower compute (automate in routing policy).
Notes for SE: list model variants and expected qualitative impact; include sample routing config snippet in Confluence page INF-RESCUE-2026.

Slide 6 — Cost comparison mini-math (talk track + numbers to show)
- Example workload: 200k monthly requests, avg 800 tokens/request -> 160M tokens/month.
- Hosted estimate: $A per 1M tokens -> monthly cost = calc (replace A during call).
- Dedicated reserved estimate: committed baseline + lower per-token unit -> show scenarios: 3mo trial vs 12mo commit.
- Upsell moment: show break-even month for reserved at current telemetry.

Slide 7 — Regulatory/Private pilot framing (sales hook)
- If customer raises data residency or auditability: propose 4-week Private pilot (VPC) -> collect logs/audit + KMS integration.
- Checklist for Private readiness: infra contacts, IP allowlist, compliance reviewers, dev/test dataset availability.
- Value props: audit logs, no-egress to public internet, optional on-prem packaging.

Slide 8 — Objection playbook (short scripts)
1) "Too expensive" -> "Let's run a focused token reduction + caching experiment for 2 weeks; if it doesn't reduce costs by >=X%, we'll propose a Dedicated pricing model with a cost guarantee."
2) "Latency spikes" -> "We can run canary routing and guarantee a 7-day SLA on the fallback pool while we root cause."
3) "We can't share telemetry" -> "We can do a collab session where you share sanitized traces; if needed, provide an on-site SE session under NDA or do a Private pilot."

Slide 9 — Demo checklist (to run live)
- Pre-call: create demo tenant with identical model variant and synthetic traffic that mirrors their average tokens and QPS.
- Show: baseline latency, enable prefix cache, re-run synthetic traffic, show delta.
- Show fallback policy in console: change routing to Dedicated/Lower-cost model and switch back.
- Capture screenshots and attach to the follow-up email.

Slide 10 — Escalation matrix (who to ping, when)
- T+0–24h: AE + field SE to own customer comms.
- T+24–48h: Eng on-call for Serving Runtime (pager: eng-sre on-call) if root cause looks infra-related.
- T+48–72h: Solutions Eng + Applied ML for model/quantization changes.
- Internal shortcut: if customer expresses churn risk in next 30 days, escalate to GTM leadership (cc: Head of Sales).
Contact hints: use Slack #field-rescue for synchronous patches; include JIRA GTMSUP-3421 in all updates.

Slide 11 — Quick email templates (copy/paste)
- Immediate follow-up after 20-min call: "Thanks — recap + agreed 48h action plan" (short bullets + attachments).
- After mitigation test: "Results + recommendation" (show numbers, next formal offer: Dedicated trial / Private pilot).
- Renewal/commit ask template: "Given our test showed X% latency reduction and Y% token reduction, can we commit to a 3-month reserved trial?"

Slide 12 — Risk to convert: timing & procurement tips
- Procurement note: reserved contracts need 3–4 week lead for procurement + finance signatures at midmarket.
- Sticky conversion levers: pilot success metrics (latency p95, cost per 1k tokens, availability), and short SLA bump for Dedicated trials.
- Ask for commitment: include a conditional clause to convert trial credits to reserved capacity if metrics met.

Slide 13 — Companion artifacts (where to find the deep links)
- Confluence: INF-RESCUE-2026 (playbook + routing examples)
- Demo tenant: demo/rapid-rescue/region-us-west (ask infra to provision)
- JIRA: GTMSUP-3421 (customer: AcmeCorp placeholder)
- Field kit: /go-to-market/field-kits/rescue-checklist.csv (attach screenshots)

Slide 14 — Postmortem template (capture in CONFLUENCE)
- Summary: one-line problem statement.
- Timeline: events T0..Tn.
- Root cause hypothesis + evidence.
- Mitigations applied and impact numbers.
- Action owners + deadlines.
- Customer sentiment + next steps for success plan.

Slide 15 — Open questions & product asks (send to Product/Applied ML)
- Auto-telemetry sampler that masks PII but preserves perf distributions.
- One-click private pilot provisioning (reduce infra lead time from weeks to days).
- Routing-dashboard: show live cost delta if you switch to fallback model.
- Request: prioritize JIRA INF-3810 (canary auto-fallback heatmap).

Appendix: quick rebut bullets vs common competitors
- Competitor A: lower latency at cost of model precision -> reply: "We offer routing + quantization profiles so you can tune per-route quality guarantees."
- Competitor B: promises on-prem but long lead time -> reply: "Private pilot template reduces time to first audit by provisioning standard artifacts up front."

End of deck
